主要内容: On March 9, 2022, Paul Munter, Acting Chief Accountant, emphasized the SEC's focus on materiality in financial reporting. Materiality is defined as errors that could significantly affect investor decisions, assessed through quantitative and qualitative factors. The SEC noted an increase in 'little r' restatements, attributed to improved internal controls and audit quality. It warned against biased materiality analyses that may lead to such restatements. The SEC stressed that accounting errors under GAAP or IFRS are relevant to investors, rejecting claims of irrelevance. Auditors must assess uncorrected misstatements and ensure quality control systems support compliance. The statement clarified it is not a rule or regulation and has no legal force. It defined an error in previously issued financial statements as an error in recognition, measurement, presentation, or disclosure due to mathematical mistakes, misapplication of GAAP, or oversight or misuse of facts. The OCA referenced legal precedents and accounting standards to guide materiality assessments, emphasizing the importance of high-quality financial information for investors.
